SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. File No. No. D 4791. SECTION 2 Date 24 April 33）
Date April 22, 1933

Subject (in full) Enquiry re: V.I.Bondareff, labourer in the Russian Labour Com-
pany attached to R.A.S.C. Supply Depot, Tifeng Road.

Made by D.S.Prokofiev. Forwarded by [签名]

Lieutenant R.B. Boulter attached to R.A.S.C. Supply Depot,
Tifeng Road, came to this office on March 27, 1933, in company with
I.Filatoff, Russian foreman-interpreter in the Russian Labour
Company attached to the above mentioned Depot, and requested in-
formation regarding a labourer in the Russian Labour Company named
V.I. Bondareff who, according to his information, is suspected of
being a " bolshevik".

Enquiries show that Bondareff arrived in Shanghai from Har-
bin in August 1927. When registering with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, No 6-A Hongkong Road, he gave the following particulars:-
" Vassily Ivanovitch Bondareff, Russian, born February 4, 1895, in
Poltava province; single; accountant; arrived in Harbin from the
U.S.S.R. in 1923".

In Shanghai he was unable to find any work, other than casual,
until September 1930 when, through the medium of the Russian Emi-
grants' Committee, he joined the Russian Labour Company attached to
R.A.S.C. Supply Depot, Tifeng Road. In December 1931, in view of
expected reduction in the staff of the company, he applied for
registration as a candidate for the post of police watchman. On
that occasion he produced a letter of recommendation from Lieu-
tenant P.G.Lomax, R.A.S.C. ( copy attached).

Bondareff is reported to have received some education. He
speaks English a little and claims to have some knowledge of
German.

I.Filatoff, foreman-interpreter in the Russian Labour Company,
who seems to be responsible for having advised Lieutenant Boulter
regarding Bondareff's alleged bolshevist leanings, was interviewed
by the undersigned on April 11. He states that he never talked
with Bondareff on politics and, therefore, he is unable to give any

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

报告

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 刑事与特别股登记处。档案号 D 4791。第2科 日期 1933年4月24日）
日期 1933年4月22日

事由（全称） 关于隶属于提丰路皇家陆军勤务团（R.A.S.C.）补给站的俄罗斯劳工队劳工 V.I. Bondareff 的调查。

由 D.S. Prokofiev 制作。呈送者 [签名]

隶属于提丰路皇家陆军勤务团（R.A.S.C.）补给站的 R.B. Boulter 中尉，于1933年3月27日，会同上述补给站所属俄罗斯劳工队的俄籍工头兼翻译 I. Filatoff 来到本办公室，请求提供关于该俄罗斯劳工队一名名为 V.I. Bondareff 的劳工的信息，据其所知，此人涉嫌为“布尔什维克”。

调查显示，Bondareff 于1927年8月从哈尔滨抵达上海。在香港路6-A号俄罗斯侨民委员会登记时，他提供了以下个人资料：“Vassily Ivanovitch Bondareff，俄国人，1895年2月4日出生于波尔塔瓦省；未婚；会计师；1923年从苏联抵达哈尔滨”。

在上海，除临时性工作外，他一直未能找到任何工作，直到1930年9月，通过俄罗斯侨民委员会的介绍，他加入了隶属于提丰路皇家陆军勤务团（R.A.S.C.）补给站的俄罗斯劳工队。1931年12月，鉴于该队人员预计裁减，他申请登记为警署巡捕候选人。当时他出示了皇家陆军勤务团（R.A.S.C.）P.G. Lomax 中尉的一封推荐信（副本附后）。

据报道，Bondareff 受过一定教育。他会说一点英语，并声称懂一些德语。

俄罗斯劳工队的工头兼翻译 I. Filatoff 似乎曾就 Bondareff 涉嫌倾向布尔什维克一事向 Boulter 中尉提出建议，本人于4月11日对其进行了问话。他表示自己从未与 Bondareff 谈论过政治，因此无法提供任何

other labourers that in casual conversations with them Bondareff

Bayasitoff and Korotkoff, labourers in the Russian Labour
Company who, according to Filatoff, could corroborate his state-
ment were interviewed on April 12 and 21 respectively. Both deny
having ever heard from Bondareff anything which could prove his
pro-Bolshevist attitude.
Information from another source indicates that Bondareff's
attitude towards the old regime in Russia and the "White" move-
ment is different from that of an average "White", and that
he may be described as a socialist without, however, any bolshe-
vist tendencies.
Nothing detrimental is known in this office regarding Bonda-
reff.
It is not unlikely that the allegations against Bondareff
are an outcome of personal antagonism between him and Filatoff.

关于
信息 ^ 此人的政治观点。然而，他觉得 Bondareff 并非真正的“白俄”。他还从其他劳工那里听说，Bondareff 在与他们的随意交谈中公开表达了对布尔什维主义的同情。
Bayasitoff 和 Korotkoff 是俄罗斯劳工队的劳工，据 Filatoff 称，他们可以佐证其说法，本人分别于4月12日和21日对他们进行了问话。两人都否认曾从 Bondareff 口中听到任何能证明其亲布尔什维克态度的言论。
来自另一来源的信息表明，Bondareff 对俄国旧政权和“白俄”运动的态度与普通“白俄”不同，他可以被称为社会主义者，但不具有布尔什维克倾向。
本办公室未掌握有关 Bondareff 的任何不利信息。
针对 Bondareff 的指控很可能是他与 Filatoff 之间个人 antagonism（敌意/对立）的结果。
G. Prokofiew

Alexandroff 警长，

介绍 V. Bondareff 先生，他此前曾得到

page_data.en:
Copy.

Headquarters,
British Troops,
Yu Yuen Camp,
Shanghai.

31st October 1931.

Dear O'Toole

I wonder could you do anything to help the writer
of the attched request.

He is a labourer in the Russian Labour Company which
is employed under my Corps.

I would like to help him as he is a good fellow, and
during the ten months he has worked under me, I can vouch for
him in all respects. He is clean, honest, trustworthy, sober and
truthful. He is also of good physique.

Owing to the economy axe his continued employment is
in jeopardy. Reductions are being effected according to service,
and any further cuts will possibly hit Bondareff.

I can also state he is hardworking and industrious,
and to my mind superior to labouring work.

If an interview was desired I would allow him off
duty to attend.

I leave for Tientsin on 26th Nov., but if it is desired
to write to Bondareff after that date the following address will
find him:-
C/o Russian Labour Company,
Supply Depot R.A.S.C.
Tifeng Road Camp,
Shanghai.

He must have got the attached written for him as his
English is much below the standard of the application.

Trusting yourself and family are keeping well and that
I may drop across you one day soon.

Yours sincerely,
p
G.G.Lomax.
Lieut.
R.A.S.C.

D.C.( Divs.)
Sir,
You may be able to place the man as Bodyguard or
Watchman. J.O'Tool D.O."C" 5/II
page_data.zh:
副本。

总部，
驻沪英军，
豫园营房，
上海。

1931年10月31日。

亲爱的 O'Toole：

不知您能否协助处理附件申请书的撰写人。

他是受我团雇用的俄罗斯劳工队的一名劳工。

我愿意帮助他，因为他是个好人，在他为我工作的十个月里，我可以各方面为他担保。他爱干净、诚实、可靠、 sober（清醒/不酗酒）且真诚。他的体格也很好。

由于削减开支，他的继续雇用面临危险。裁员正根据服役情况进行，进一步的裁减可能会影响到 Bondareff。

我还可以说，他工作努力、勤奋，在我看来，他的能力高于普通劳工工作。

如果需要面谈，我可以准假让他前来。

我将于11月26日前往天津，但如果在此日期之后需要写信给 Bondareff，可以通过以下地址找到他：
转交上海提丰路营房
皇家陆军勤务团（R.A.S.C.）补给站
俄罗斯劳工队

附件中的申请书一定是别人代写的，因为他的英语水平远低于申请书的水平。

相信您和家人一切安好，希望不久能与您偶遇。

您真诚的，
p
G.G. Lomax.
中尉
皇家陆军勤务团（R.A.S.C.）

各师副指挥官（D.C. (Divs.)）
先生，
您或许能将此人安置为保镖或巡捕。 J. O'Tool 副指挥官（D.O."C"） 11月5日

page_data.en:
Copy.

The Officer i/c Barracks,
Shanghai,

27th October, 1931.

Lieut. P.G. Lomax, M.B.E.

Dear Sir,

Although I am not to be discharged for reason of the
decrease of staff, yet because of the different misunderstandings
between myself and my minor superiors I would like to change my
job.

As you have always been very kind and considerate to me I
beg you to be so kind as to give me a letter to the Chief of the
Municipal Police, stating that I am working at your place, and that
you have known me for over a year for quite a respectable man,
but because of the decrease of staff I may have to leave at any
time; and would he be able to offer me some job as a bodyguard.
As far as I know, nearly every month some Russians are taken on for
this kind of work, and the wages are more than what I am earning
at present. This will give me a chance to save some money and enable
me to leave Shanghai.

If you cannot give me a letter or introduction to the Chief
of Police, perhaps you would be so kind as to go with me to see
him, and recommend me. This as it may please you.

I am asking you this favour because you know me, and I have
worked under you. I beg you to excuse me for troubling you, and
thank you very much for all that you have done for me, and for
all that it may please you to do for me in the future.

I ask you this in writing because I am not able to speak to
you and tell you what I want.

I am, Sir,
Your faithful and obedient servant,

( Signed ) V. Bondareff.
page_data.zh:
副本。

致上海营房主管军官，

1931年10月27日。

P.G. Lomax 中尉，大英帝国勋章获得者（M.B.E.）

尊敬的先生：

虽然我并非因人员减少而被解雇，但由于我与下级上司之间存在种种误会，我希望调换工作。

鉴于您一直对我非常友善和体贴，我恳请您惠赐一封致警务处处长的信函，说明我在您处工作，且您认识我已有一年多，认为我是一个相当体面的人，但由于人员减少，我可能随时不得不离开；询问他是否能给我提供一份保镖之类的工作。据我所知，几乎每个月都有俄国人被录用从事此类工作，且工资比我目前的收入更高。这将使我有机会积蓄一些钱，并使我能够离开上海。

如果您不能给我出具致警务处处长的信函或引荐信，也许您可以好心地陪我一起去见他，并推荐我。此事悉听尊便。

我向您提出这一请求，是因为您了解我，且我曾为您工作。恳请原谅我的打扰，并非常感谢您为我所做的一切，以及将来可能为我做的一切。

我以书面形式提出此请求，因为我无法当面与您交谈并告诉您我的需求。

先生，我是
您忠诚顺仆，

（签名） V. Bondareff.
